title: Validity of a linear-check seed
statement: Let $w$ be a Boolean word of length $n$, let $P$ be a Boolean proof word of length $n+2(n+1)$, and let a seed be either an endpoint check or a position $i<n$ paired with a transition check. The seed holds of $P$ and $w$ precisely under the corresponding condition: the false endpoint check requires the linear-prefix proof bit at index $0$ to be false; the true endpoint check requires the quadratic-prefix proof bit at index $0$ to be false; the other endpoint check requires the quadratic-prefix proof bit at index $n$ to be true. At a position $i$, the false transition check requires the linear-prefix proof bits at $i$ and $i+1$ to sum with $w_i$ to zero in $\mathbb F_2$; the true transition check requires the product proof bit to equal the conjunction of the linear-prefix proof bit at $i$ and $w_i$; and the remaining transition check requires the quadratic-prefix proof bits at $i$ and $i+1$ to sum with the product proof bit at $i$ to zero in $\mathbb F_2$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean proof word of length $n+2(n+1)$
A seed of the specified endpoint-or-position form
caveat: The auxiliary prefix-bit functions, product-proof indices, and Boolean-to-$\mathbb F_2$ encoding are not defined in the supplied material.
